sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020 [title page: Edition IV, 2019]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th edition. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 198 pp. Entry 413 'Shamang', p. 89.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: per-language index entry only (names, location, classification, sources). It establishes that the only Shamang material known to Blench is his own unpublished 2016 wordlist; no grammar, phonology, survey or thesis is listed for Shamang (contrast Hyam cluster entry 182 with alphabet chart 1999 and scripture 1923).
sources.venue: An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th edition

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. Research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 3-44. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.209
sources.note: Nothing. Shamang occurs only in Table 2 (p. 10: no literacy/scripture/media) and in the Hyamic membership list (p. 21); p. 21: 'Apart from Hyam of Kwoi, these languages remain very poorly known (see Jockers 1982).' The words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the article.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 107-172. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1314325
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Shamang: Table 3 p. 115 'As Hyam cluster'; §2.3.5 p. 131 lists Shamang under Hyamic and says 'Many of these languages are very poorly known and existing descriptions are tonally and phonologically inadequate (e.g. Dihoff 1976; Jockers 1982).. Analysis of Hyamic languages is based solely on fieldwork by the author.' Only a family-level remark p. 111: 'Most Plateau languages have a three-level tone system'. No Shamang forms given.
Nothing; stub says only 'a poorly known Plateau language of Nigeria', cites Glottolog; Central Plateau page cites Blench 2018, Blench 2019 Atlas (4th ed.), Blench 2008 'Prospecting proto-Plateau'.
